activity.notes: The Capitulation of Toledo in 1529 appointed Francisco Pizarro governor and captain general of the territories officially designated New Castile. The grant preceded the actual conquest of the Inca heartland, which began in earnest in 1532, but it constituted his formal colonial governing commission. He remained the central Spanish governor in Peru until his assassination in Lima in 1541. ATLAS does not attach him to the Inca Empire as if he served or ruled that polity.

sources.title: Francisco Pizarro — Treccani
sources.citation_text: Treccani states that the 1529 capitulations named Pizarro captain general and governor of the new territories officially called New Castile and records his death in 1541.

sources.title: Royal provisions granting titles to Francisco Pizarro — PARES, Archivo General de Indias
sources.citation_text: The Spanish state archive catalogs the royal provisions granting Pizarro the titles of governor, adelantado and captain general, dated after 26 July 1529.
